title: Replicate the f35v motif scores with independent masked annotators
statement: An outline checklist applied to 12 caption-masked illustrations from three manuscripts in the Tractatus de herbis tradition gives full fruit scores to both black-ivy plates, both elder plates, one bryony plate and both Sloane grape views. The Egerton galla tree best reproduces the combination of offset rounded-lobed side leaves and compact crown. BnF galla and glandes also carry rounded lobing, with cupped fruits on all three oak plates. No comparator visibly meets the doubled aerial crossing or hooked, strongly asymmetric root criteria, and all match at most seven of the 12 features even if uncertain features count as matches. The black-ivy fruit parallel and oak foliage parallel are regional correspondences, with insufficient specificity for a botanical anchor.
check: Give the frozen outline rubric and randomly coded crops to two observers who have not seen the proposed identifications, with headings masked by a separate preparer. Compare calls region by region before revealing the panel identities. Confirm whether two oak leaves genuinely sit below the crown, adjudicate the clipped roots, and report exact agreement and sensitivity to omitting F2 and C3. Treat the three manuscripts as related witnesses and use no Voynich label or proposed text.

evidence.method: One observer fixed the checklist after seeing Yale f35v and the published BnF ivy comparator but before opening the other images. The same observer located and masked headings and then scored shuffled codes. Familiar shapes and preparation exposed specimen identities in some cases. The experiment is caption-masked with incomplete observer blinding. Residual prose beside contours can remain. Counts record depiction only. Separate cuttings and their crossings were never pooled into a single plant. The BnF vine occupies a two-page card with the center gutter. The abbreviated Sloane grape plate adds a second depiction from the same witness. The f60v eleborum illustration, Egerton f46r Herba vitis illustration of a distinct herb, and Sloane f102v plate without the designated Bryonia heading were not treated as substitutes for the named entries.
evidence.rubric:
# Public f35v motif comparison, fixed before opening the additional plates

Previously seen: Beinecke f35v, the black-ivy detail and Ethel Voynich oak-grape note reproduced on p. 24 of Zandbergen's 2012 slides, and full BnF latin 6823 f60r. Expected familiarity with ordinary silhouettes of the named plants. New comparator categories fixed using headings and documented plant names only. Use two compact Tractatus de herbis witnesses as available, Latin 6823 and Egerton 747, preferentially both witnesses per group. Seek the named black ivy and oak/gall tree, with three depicted alternatives (grape, elder and a lobed-leaf rooted herb, white bryony where catalogued). Where the requested entry has multiple drawings, retain all candidates or use separately illustrated entries if the source distinguishes them before viewing, rather than pick a nearest shape. Keep captions and neighboring plants outside the illustration where possible. When contours touch words, neutral mask the text without removing contours and log the exception. Record plates under shuffled codes before joining the identities. This is caption-masked, with one observer and incomplete blinding.

Use only outlines of the drawing: color may locate a contour, but it earns no points. For each feature use 1 visible, 0 visibly discordant or visibly missing on a complete plate, ? genuinely ambiguous or cropped. Record all 12 codes and matched count per region, with possible upper counts for unknowns. Equal weights; no hypothesis test. Describe where matches arise. Multiple manuscripts can transmit a drawing tradition, so report each witness without treating them as independent statistical draws.

Fruit (F)
F1. At least two discrete clusters of three or more rounded enclosed units, counting each unit once; scattered solitary fruits do not count.
F2. At least one such cluster terminates a distinct stalk, with recognizable grouping and no enclosing common fruit body or backing leaf.
F3. No acorn-like cup, enclosing husk, or lobed capsule around the rounded units; mark unknown if outlines are unreadable, zero if no rounded units.

Leaf (L)
L1. At least two individually outlined side leaves attach at distinct levels below the top foliage.
L2. Those side leaves are simple and visibly lobed, with at least two broad rounded lobes per side.
L3. The strongest lobing repeats along the long axis on both sides of the leaf; do not count a three- to five-point palmate leaf, a smooth small leaf, or individual leaflets along a rachis.

Crown/stems (C)
C1. A compact upper foliage outline distinguishable from lower lateral leaves or fruit.
C2. Multiple upward stalks fan toward that upper outline from a relatively narrow common point or band.
C3. Two lower lateral stems visibly cross in front of or around a distinct upright axis; a single fork without crossing does not count.

Roots (R)
R1. Clearly drawn roots and aerial stems meet at a common basal junction.
R2. Major lateral roots or primary branches bear at least three recognizable hooked or curved tips in aggregate.
R3. Strongly asymmetric lateral spread, roughly 2:1 or greater from the stem center measured against opposite side, with the longest root roughly horizontal for much of its run.

For a caption-free target, all 12 features are the prespecified matches; F2 and C3 will also be reported under a sensitivity analysis dropping either if attachment or topology proves uncertain on the scan. The rubric is target-conditioned, so results test specificity among documented controls, not identification in the abstract.
evidence.scoring_key: Per card and region, 1 is visible correspondence, 0 is absent or discordant, ? is obscured or ambiguous. Range counts definite to possible matches.
evidence.mask_spec: Coordinates are XYXY in pixels at reference dimensions. Cover rectangles in warm grey RGB (228,225,215), leaving the rest unchanged. Crop rectangles, juxtapose adjacent halves where applicable, then keep within 800 x 720 pixels. Seed 3506823 sets the order for the recorded preparation. At decision points where the crop concealed a contour, compare the full scan after the masked pass.
evidence.sensitivity: Dropping F2 changes fruit-perfect controls from 7 of 12 with 3/3 to the same 7 with 2/2. Dropping C3 preserves all control ranks because C3 is zero for every control. Dropping either criterion leaves the region split unchanged. Ignoring the side-leaf position requirement would raise the foliage match for Latin 6823 galla and glandes because the rounded lobes are visible elsewhere in their drawings.

cards.plate: BL Sloane MS 4016 f101r (three illustrated cuttings)
cards.heading: Vitis communis, agrestis and nigra
cards.notes: Clustered units on peduncles; pointed palmate blades and curling tendrils; two separate cuttings cross but there is no third shared upright axis or common base.

cards.heading: Voynich f35v
cards.notes: Comparison target; two lateral round-lobed blades at different heights; root spread measured about 2.5 times farther to the left than to the right of the main stem.

cards.plate: BnF Latin 6823 ff164v–165r (sinuous axis through gutter)
cards.heading: Vitis
cards.notes: Continuous sinuous woody axis and tendrils spanning two pages; no separate rounded units securely visible; lower drawing ends in a cut or tapered axis.

cards.heading: Edera nigra
cards.notes: Small clustered units, triangular to angular leaves; the lower axis reaches the page edge, excluding a root assessment.

cards.heading: Galla
cards.notes: Occupied cups and separate round spots in a compact rounded-leaf upper crown; no securely isolated below-crown side pair; lower lines near the base are faint and may include neighboring plant marks.

cards.heading: Brionia / Vitis alba
cards.notes: Open radial groups of small rounds, broad angular blades, two long divergent tapering portions of a single large root body.

cards.plate: BnF Latin 6823 f63v (large plant at left)
cards.heading: Ebulus
cards.notes: Small outlined units in hemispherical heads on a tall pinnate pattern; roots extend to page edges and their terminal topology and ratio are uncertain.

cards.heading: Uva minoris
cards.notes: Compact drooping bunches, pointed leaves on a curved axis, and no common roots in the depicted cutting.

cards.heading: Glandes
cards.notes: Cupped fruits and visibly rounded lobes on a short twig; no two isolated lower blades below a crown and no root.

cards.heading: Galla
cards.notes: Separated lower lobed blades feed a near-compact canopy with curled upper edges; cups flank free oval spots; basal roots spread mainly downward with no three hooked tips visible.

cards.heading: Ebulus
cards.notes: Open small rounded units arranged at radial stalk ends; repeating pinnate stem tiers; crossing branches belong to its root system, not aerial side stems.

cards.heading: Brionia
cards.notes: Scattered uncapped round units at leaf bases, no two clusters; long bifurcating root without asymmetric horizontal spread.

cards.heading: Edera nigra
cards.notes: Uncapped small clusters and angled to cordate leaves; a faint basal junction is visible on the full scan; a single winding support/axis does not meet the specified doubled crossing.
